correctness.rationale: For n=2m+1>=5, the opposite support face of each edge is a vertex, so the edge-vertex triangle representation counts all affine diameters away from a finite union of segments. Along a generic ray, each triangle is exited once and each longest-diagonal boundary removes exactly two memberships; the count descends from n to 1 in steps of two. The intersection of all triangles is bounded by the n equally spaced center-side halfplanes of the longest diagonals. Each such line is at distance R sin(pi/(2n)); the central regular n-gon's circumradius is that distance divided by cos(pi/n). The area ratio is the square of the circumradius ratio. The proof handles the full infinite quantifier analytically, not by finite enumeration.

value.rationale: Affine-diameter multiplicity is a classical incidence invariant, and the maximum-level set is a natural geometric statistic. The exact area fraction tells what proportion of a uniformly chosen point lies on every affine diameter and shows a sharp quadratic n^-2 decay as regular odd polygons approach the circular regime. The infinite-family parity/support classification extends the isolated pentagon case without claiming the full intermediate-level distribution.
